title: CHAPTER FIFTEEN. On the ministry of the word: definition
pass_a_gloss: Pass A clause gloss (reordered): In Greek it stands as called diakonia, leitourgia, episkope, oikonomia; in ye Old Testament ye Levites' ministry stands as custody and warfare. Ye Fathers call it hierurgia; Paul names ministers presbyteroi. It stands as a sacred office distinct from profane and civil offices. — Ye MINISTRY OF THE WORD stands as a sacred office enjoined by God through lawful calling on fit persons, that by teaching His word, administering ye sacraments, and absolving and binding, they may call and direct people toward God's kingdom and salvation. — CHAPTER FIFTEEN. On ye ministry belonging toward ye word.
pass_b_english: CHAPTER FIFTEEN. On the ministry of the word.

The MINISTRY OF THE WORD is a sacred office enjoined by God through lawful calling on fit persons, that by teaching His word, administering the sacraments, and absolving and binding, they may call and direct people to God's kingdom and salvation.

In Greek it is called diakonia, leitourgia, episkope, oikonomia; in the Old Testament the Levites' ministry is custody and warfare. The Fathers call it hierurgia; Paul names ministers presbyteroi. It is a sacred office distinct from profane and civil offices.
source_text: CAPUT DECIMUM QUINTUM, De ministerio verbi. MINISTERIUM VERBI quod est officium sacrum a Deo per legitimam vocationem idoneis personis iniunctum, ut verbum ipsius docendo, sacramenta administrando, absolvendo et ligando, homines ad regnum Dei ac salutem vocent atque dirigant. Graecis diakonia dicitur (Acts 1:17; 6:4); item leitourgia (Phil. 2:17; Rom. 15:16); episkope (Acts 1:20; 1 Tim. 3:1); oikonomia (1 Cor. 9:17; Eph. 3:2). In V.T. ministerium Levitarum dicitur custodia et militia. Patres vocant hierurgiam; quo sensu Paulo ministri sunt presbyteroi (1 Tim. 5:17). Est officium sacrum (1 Tim. 3:1) distinctum a profanis et civilibus (Matt. 26:21; Luke 22:25).
